extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations (undergraduate/graduate level and PR professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for diagnosing PR problems, designing and implementing PR programs (research, planning, messaging, implementation, evaluation), and for internal/external media relations across organizational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining Public Relations Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Problem Statement; Situation Analysis — Internal Factors; External Factors; SWOT Analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear problem statement and systematic situation analysis (consider internal and external factors and perform a SWOT) as the foundation for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Methods for Strategic Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal/Exploratory Methods: Personal contact and observation; Key informants; Focus groups; Community forums; Advisory committees and boards; Ombudsman or ombuds officer; Call-in telephone lines; Mail and email analyses; Social media and other online sources; Field reports. Formal Methods: Secondary analysis and online databases; Content analysis; Surveys (mailed, in-person, telephone, online; cross-sectional vs. trend and panel surveys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate exploratory and formal research techniques to build an information base for problem definition, target-public analysis, and evaluation; understand tradeoffs (depth, representativeness, cost).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Relations Goals and Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Relations Goals; Public Relations Planning — excuses for not planning; Role of working theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set explicit goals grounded in working theory; anticipate and overcome common excuses for skipping planning to ensure coherent programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target Publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Publics Across Situations; Publics Specific to Situations; Approaches to Defining Publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and segment publics carefully (situational and enduring) using appropriate approaches so strategies and messages match audience characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Management by Objectives; Writing Program Objectives; Objectives in Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write measurable objectives (management-by-objectives approach) that link to goals and allow evaluation of outcomes in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategies and Tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Action and Communication Strategies; Action as an Open Systems Response; Action Before Communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate strategy (broad approach) from tactics (specific actions); coordinate organizational actions with communication; prioritize substantive action when appropriate before messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Relations Plan Components and Pretests
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan Components; Budgeting; Pretesting Program Elements; Getting Buy-In for the Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include defined components (objectives, strategies, tactics, timelines, budgets); pretest key program elements and secure stakeholder buy-in before full implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning for Program Implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing Planning Scenarios; Anticipating Disasters and Crises; Establishing an Information Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop implementation scenarios, contingency plans for crises, and centralized information resources to support coordinated responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message Content — Crafting the Message
rubrics_metrics.description: Crafting the Message — Compliance-gaining strategies; Power and fear appeals; One-sided and two-sided arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appeal types and argument structure based on audience, objectives, and ethical considerations; consider potential effects of fear/power appeals and whether to present one- or two-sided arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing and Priming Messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Coorientation and Framing; Framing for News Media; Priming for Effective Framing; More Framing Tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame messages to align perceived issue perspectives between organization and publics (coorientation); tailor frames for media contexts and use priming to influence how audiences interpret issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encoding and Decoding Messages
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to semantics and symbolic meanings; avoid stereotyping; find common cultural or experiential touchpoints to improve message decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message Delivery and Channel Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Disseminating Messages; Selecting Delivery Channels — Sources of Influence; Opinion Leaders; Using Special Events; Adapting to New Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose channels and intermediaries (opinion leaders, events) that maximize reach and credibility; adapt tactics for converging and new media platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers to Implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience Obstacles; Speaker Obstacles; Subject and Purpose Obstacles; Diffusion Obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and mitigate obstacles in audiences (attention, values), speakers (credibility, clarity), subject/purpose (complexity, relevance), and diffusion (spread of innovation) to improve implementation success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis Communication (planning and response as a specific program element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare specialized crisis communication procedures within planning and implementation (anticipation, rapid coordinated response, information center).

rubrics_metrics.name: Levels of Program Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels: Preparation Criteria and Methods (Information Base; Program Content; Presentation Quality); Implementation Criteria and Methods (Distribution; Placement; Potential Audience; Attentive Audience); Impact Criteria and Methods (Knowledge Gain; Opinion Change; Attitude Change; Behavior Change; Repeated Behavior; Goal Achieved; Social and Cultural Change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate programs across preparation, implementation, and impact stages using the listed criteria; match methods to level (e.g., distribution/placement measures for implementation, surveys/behavioral measures for impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Research Process and Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing for Evaluation; Evaluation Research Process; Evaluation Research Steps; Interpreting and Using Results of Evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan evaluation early, follow systematic research steps, and interpret findings to inform future planning and demonstrate measurable results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Relations and Employee Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Acculturating Employees (Vision Statements; Mission Statements; Policy Documents; Ethics Statements; Training Materials); Informing Employees Using Nonmediated Communication (the 'Grapevine'; Meetings, Teleconferences, and Videoconferences); Informing Employees Using Mediated Communication (Employee Publications; Inserts and Enclosures; Published Speeches, Position Papers, and Backgrounders; Bulletin Boards; Intranets; Hotlines; Email; New Media); Listening to Employees; Connecting Employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of mediated and nonmediated channels to acculturate and inform employees; include listening mechanisms and connection strategies to maintain internal engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Media and Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional Media (newspapers, wire services, magazines, radio, television, cable); New Media and Challenges (staying abreast of technology, global transparency, media convergence, new media players); Representing Organizations in Social Media; Working with the Media (Person in the Middle; Guidelines for Good Media Relations; Working with International Media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt media-relations practices to both traditional and new media contexts; follow guidelines for good media relations and designate skilled intermediaries for media interactions, including international considerations.
